title: ImageBitmapRenderingContext: clarify behaviour with `premultiplyAlpha: "none"` createImageBitmap option and canvas
body:
### What is the issue with the HTML Standard?

While trying to understand how to correctly pass an RGBA image through canvas and back out as PNG with a correct un-premultiplied workflow, I encountered several implementation issues (WebKit, Firefox) that lead me to believe the spec is not quite clear around how a `premultiplyAlpha: none` workflow works together with `ImageBitmapRenderingContext`.

I'm not entirely sure what the missingpiece of information is, but
- https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#the-imagebitmaprenderingcontext-interface does not have any notes in regard to what options have been set on the canvas and the ImageData – the _size_ of the canvas changes since that points at the new image, and I guess the same happens for `alpha: true | false` depending on the ImageBitmap data, but it's not clearly defined if `premultiplyAlpha: none` from ImageData still applies. 
- when then converting the canvas back to PNG (e.g. canvas.toDataURL("image/png")) implementations seem to disagree on whether the `premultiplyAlpha: none` option should still be respected; Chrome respects it (resulting in correct RGBA data being returned) whereas both WebKit and Firefox ignore it.

I wasn't able to understand from the spec what the correct behaviour is, and what the correct approach is for reading back that kind of data in a correct fashion.

I set up a reproduction page for the unclarity here with some examples:
https://unpremultiplied-readback.glitch.me/
